clue.text: Indication of failure the minute general's been felled

parts.note: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of the tiny nineteenth-century showman Charles Stratton, so the minute general's name gives these letters
something felled has been knocked to the ground, so it is down

explanation.surface: A small army officer has fallen, which looks like a sign that something has gone wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The minute general' is a famous little man, General Tom Thumb, whose stage title the clue borrows; read the possessive as 'Thumb is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A downturned fist with the digit pointing at the floor is the familiar gesture of rejection or failure.

clue.text: Modicum of perceptiveness providing partial opening?

definitions.meaning: keeping a little attention on something, only partly watching it
an eye is an opening, so a fraction of one is a partial opening

explanation.surface: Someone asks how much insight a slightly open door would give.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means watching with slight attention; literally a fractional portion of an organ of sight.

clue.text: Main associate of a child, say

indicators.note: say tells us to take the sound of the words a child, not their spelling

parts.note: a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: Asking who a child's chief companion is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' is not 'chief' here: in the phrase 'with ___ and main' the two words are paired, so the definition is main's partner word.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'with might and main' pairs the two words, both meaning strength, so one is the other's associate.

clue.text: Applies grease over every one of the weapons

indicators.note: over says the first piece is placed over, around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: to smarm is to smooth down hair with grease or oil
every one means all

explanation.surface: Someone oils each of the guns in an armoury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Applies grease' looks like gun maintenance, but it means smoothing hair with oil, and 'over' wraps it round the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Small arms are pistols, rifles and other hand-held firearms, a class of weapons.

clue.text: Eccentric Chinaman, perhaps

definitions.meaning: in cricket a chinaman is an unusual delivery, a left-arm wrist spinner's off-break, so an odd kind of ball

explanation.surface: A strange person from China is the image, which the cricket sense undoes.
explanation.walkthrough: A chinaman is a cricket term for a left-arm bowler's wrist-spun delivery, so it is literally an unusual ball.
explanation.definitionFit: An odd or unconventional person is called a crank or oddity, and the cricket delivery is an unusual ball.

clue.text: Snow runs? Surely not!

parts.note: névé is granular snow on the upper part of a glacier
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone hears that snow is flowing and protests in disbelief.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of disbelief is like 'no way', meaning at no time.

clue.text: Key one needed for clock

parts.note: F is a musical key
an ace is the one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A single key is required to wind a clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is the slang verb meaning to see or confront, not the timepiece, though the answer is also part of a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: In slang, to clock someone is to notice or confront them, as when you stand up to a person.

clue.text: Identify the point from which prints may be taken

definitions.text: from which prints may be taken

parts.note: to finger someone is to identify them to the police
a tip is a point or extreme end

explanation.surface: A detective works out the spot where fingerprints can be lifted.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingerprints are taken by pressing the pad at the end of each digit onto ink and card.

clue.text: Prepared to break in to find what's in container

definitions.meaning: burglars who have ... a building have looked it over beforehand
something put inside a box or sheath is enclosed in one

explanation.surface: A burglar gets ready to break in and see what is inside a box.
explanation.definitionFit: Thieves who have reconnoitred a property have scouted it; an object in a box or sheath is encased.

clue.text: Idler finally starting to pull in both directions

annotationWithheld.why: Idler finally starting to pull in both directions (8): LUG + GARD (DRAG backwards) give pull in both directions, but no reading of 'finally starting' yields the opening S
annotationWithheld.clue: Idler finally starting to pull in both directions

clue.text: Suddenly leave from the front is hard to get

parts.note: the van is the front of an army or procession
H is the abbreviation for hard on pencils

explanation.surface: Someone notes that exiting at the front is difficult.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear abruptly is to depart without warning, out of sight in an instant.

clue.text: Long pair of shorts?

parts.note: in verse a metrical foot of one long syllable followed by two short ones is a long and a pair of shorts

explanation.surface: Someone asks for shorts that are long, trousers really.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shorts' are short syllables, not clothing; prosody marks syllables as long or short.
explanation.definitionFit: This metrical foot is one stressed syllable then two unstressed, as in 'Washington', the long-short-short pattern.

clue.text: Simpletons unexpectedly had raise

indicators.note: unexpectedly suggests things turn out in an unforeseen way, so the words had raise are jumbled

explanation.surface: Fools were surprised to get a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Empty-headed, silly people are called simpletons, as if their skulls held nothing.

clue.text: Distinctive tendency to be conceited, say

indicators.note: say tells us to hear the word for conceited rather than read it

parts.note: conceited means vain

explanation.surface: A person has a marked habit of being self-important.
explanation.definitionFit: A vein of humour or melancholy is a strain or characteristic streak in someone's manner.

clue.text: One acts on impulse with courage to take on political group

parts.note: nerve means courage or daring
a cell is a small group of activists in a political movement

explanation.surface: A brave impulsive person joins a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acts on impulse' suggests a rash person; it is the electrical impulse a neuron carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A neuron transmits electrical impulses through the body, so it acts on impulses.

clue.text: Story about, for instance, being sent down

indicators.note: about places the first piece around the second, enclosing it

parts.note: a relation is a narration or account

explanation.surface: A tale of someone, for example, being expelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Relegation is demotion to a lower division, as a football club drops down a league.

clue.text: It's naive to support the dollar

parts.note: green means inexperienced or naive
to back is to support

explanation.surface: It is innocent to prop up the American currency.
explanation.definitionFit: US paper currency has green reverses, giving the slang name for a banknote of that country.

clue.text: Goes round with completed tarts king's consumed

parts.note: out can mean finished or brought to an end

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed up, so the tarts take the letter inside them

parts.note: flans are open tarts
K is the chess abbreviation for king; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone circles round, having finished tarts the king has eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: To get past the side of an enemy force is to go around its wing.

clue.text: Viola, here's a seat, specially for you

indicators.note: specially suggests arranged for a particular purpose, so the letters of here's a seat are reordered

explanation.surface: A host offers a seat to someone called Viola.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Viola' looks like a woman's name or the instrument; it is the flower genus.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild pansy, Viola tricolor, has this old country name.

clue.text: Atrium the French covered with gold

indicators.note: in a down answer the second piece is covered by the first, which sits on top

parts.note: auric means of or containing gold
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: A grand hall in a French building is gilded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Atrium' suggests an entrance hall; it is a heart chamber.
explanation.definitionFit: Each upper chamber of the heart is called an atrium, from its ear-shaped appendage.

clue.text: Spread intelligence

definitions.meaning: a savoury paste spread on toast
the head, used jokily for brains

explanation.surface: Two words, a picnic paste and brain power.
explanation.definitionFit: A meat paste for toast is one sense; the crown of the head, standing for brains, the other.

clue.text: Bear in mind part of army given honour by Queen

parts.note: REME, the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, is a corps of the British Army
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour
R, for Regina, means queen

explanation.surface: A soldier's unit is honoured by the monarch, to be kept in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in your thoughts is to recall or not forget it.

clue.text: Wise picker of winners

parts.note: both the comedian partner of Eric Morecambe, surnamed Wise, and the British premium bond machine that randomly selects prize-winning numbers

explanation.surface: A shrewd tipster chooses winners.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings lottery; the computer drawing their winners has the same name as half of comedy duo Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to the Morecambe and Wise comedian and to the random number machine drawing Premium Bond prizes.

clue.text: Spartan is in vehicle that's overturned

indicators.note: overturned in a down answer means the whole assembly is turned upside down, read from bottom to top
in places the word is inside the vehicle

parts.note: a cab is a vehicle, a taxi

explanation.surface: A man from Sparta sits in a car that has rolled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spartan' looks like a person from Sparta; it is the adjective meaning austere.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartan means plain and austere, providing only the essentials.

clue.text: Almost noon? Too soon

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is almost midday and is told it is premature.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost means not quite, all but.

clue.text: Pinafore" being performed after a month

indicators.note: after places the performance piece after the month

parts.note: Apr is the abbreviation for April
a play being performed is on

explanation.surface: HMS Pinafore, the operetta, is staged a month later.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the Gilbert and Sullivan operetta HMS Pinafore; the definition is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless garment worn over clothes to protect them, like a smock.

clue.text: Knight in glossy attire, going backwards, shows reverence

indicators.note: going backwards means the knight-in-glossy assembly is read from right to left
in, with attire, says the knight is dressed inside the other piece
attire suggests clothing, so the glossy piece wraps round the knight

parts.note: sleek means smooth and glossy
N is the chess abbreviation for knight

explanation.surface: A knight in shining armour retreats and bows in respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Going down on one's knees is a gesture of homage or worship.

clue.text: Presiding over church publication

parts.note: an airing is a making public of something

explanation.surface: Someone runs a church newsletter.
explanation.definitionFit: Running a meeting as its president is presiding over it.

clue.text: End part of list

definitions.meaning: the end crust of a loaf, or the back of a foot or shoe
of a ship, to lean or tilt to one side

explanation.surface: The last item on a list.
explanation.definitionFit: The rind or end of a loaf is one sense; a ship that leans over to one side tilts in the same way, the other.

clue.text: Disrespect shown by English cows during game

indicators.note: during puts the cattle piece in the middle of the game

parts.note: chess is a game
kine is an old plural of cow

explanation.surface: English cattle behave rudely while a game is going on.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudence or lack of respect is shown by lippy, insolent behaviour.
